tutorials.title: Getting Started ESP32 and Node-RED
tutorials.mainRecommendation: Replace the deprecated node-red-dashboard with FlowFuse Dashboard 2.0, and update MQTT broker recommendations due to HiveMQ public broker reliability issues.

topIssues.title: node-red-dashboard Deprecated
topIssues.description: The tutorial instructs users to install node-red-dashboard which has been formally deprecated with no further development planned.
topIssues.recommendation: Replace with FlowFuse Dashboard 2.0 (@flowfuse/node-red-dashboard)

topIssues.title: HiveMQ Public Broker Reliability
topIssues.description: The tutorial uses broker.hivemq.com which has documented reliability issues including rate limiting, random disconnections, and overload problems.
topIssues.recommendation: Recommend HiveMQ Cloud free tier or self-hosted Mosquitto as alternatives

topIssues.title: Node-RED Version Requirements Changed
topIssues.description: Current Node-RED 5.0 requires Node.js 22.9.0 minimum (24.x recommended), which may conflict with older installation instructions.
topIssues.recommendation: Update version requirements to Node.js 22.9.0+ and Node-RED 5.x

topIssues.title: Unnecessary MQTT Broker Package
topIssues.description: The tutorial may instruct installing node-red-contrib-mqtt-broker which is unnecessary as MQTT nodes are built into Node-RED.
topIssues.recommendation: Remove or clarify that built-in MQTT nodes are sufficient

topIssues.title: EspMQTTClient Library Alternatives
topIssues.description: While EspMQTTClient still works, newer alternatives like ESP32MQTTClient offer better thread-safety and ESP32 Arduino Core 3.x compatibility.
topIssues.recommendation: Optionally mention ESP32MQTTClient as a modern alternative

keep.reason: The ESP32 board setup and pin connections remain valid
ESP32 board package installation process is still current
The explanation of MQTT publish/subscribe patterns remains accurate
The overall project architecture (ESP32 → MQTT → Node-RED → Dashboard) is still valid
The library still functions correctly for basic MQTT operations

update.action: Replace with @flowfuse/node-red-dashboard (FlowFuse Dashboard 2.0)

update.reason: HiveMQ public broker has reliability issues
update.action: Recommend HiveMQ Cloud free tier as primary option
Update to Node.js 22.9.0+ and Node-RED 5.x
Replace all UI screenshots with current versions

remove.action: Remove or clarify that this package is unnecessary
Replace with current versions or use general recommendations

evidence.finding: Documented reliability issues, rate limiting, random disconnections
Official successor with new ui-base, ui-page, ui-group structure

links.notes: Has reliability issues - rate limiting and random disconnections reported

topIssues.description: Tutorial could mention DHT22 as an alternative with better accuracy and range for users who need more precision.
topIssues.recommendation: Briefly mention DHT22 as higher-accuracy alternative

topIssues.title: Error Handling
topIssues.description: Code could include better error handling for WiFi connection failures and ThingSpeak API errors.

Working code for reading DHT11 and sending to ThingSpeak
Standard ESP32 setup process is current
ThingSpeak chart configuration remains valid

tutorials.title: Getting Started with ESP32 and Over-The-Air Programming (OTA)

topIssues.description: OTA updates are a security-sensitive feature. The tutorial should emphasize changing default credentials (admin/admin), using strong passwords, and never exposing OTA to public internet.
topIssues.recommendation: Add dedicated security section with password, network, and HTTPS guidance

topIssues.title: Default Credentials Warning
topIssues.description: The OTAWebUpdater example uses admin/admin as default username and password. This must be changed for any real-world use.
topIssues.recommendation: Add prominent warning to change credentials immediately

topIssues.title: Network Security Guidance
topIssues.description: Tutorial should advise keeping OTA devices on private networks only, and never exposing OTA ports to the internet.
topIssues.recommendation: Add note about private network use only

topIssues.title: Alternative Libraries Not Mentioned
topIssues.description: AsyncElegantOTA and other modern alternatives offer better features and security options.
topIssues.recommendation: Briefly mention AsyncElegantOTA for advanced users

topIssues.title: HTTPS Recommendation
topIssues.description: For production use, HTTPS should be recommended instead of HTTP for OTA updates.
topIssues.recommendation: Add note about HTTPS for production deployments

keep.reason: Clear explanation of how OTA works and its benefits
Walkthrough of loading OTAWebUpdater example is accurate
Instructions for setting SSID and password are correct
Accurate instructions for exporting .bin files
How to access and use the OTA web page is valid
Important note about keeping OTA code in future uploads

update.reason: OTA security is critical but not covered
update.action: Add new section on changing default credentials, network isolation, and security risks
Add prominent warning and instructions to change credentials
Note that esp32.local may not work on all networks, provide IP fallback

tutorials.title: Getting Started with FreeRTOS on ESP32
tutorials.mainRecommendation: Tutorial is technically sound. Consider adding notes about single-core ESP32 variants (ESP32-C3) compatibility and stack size best practices for beginners transitioning from the basic level.

topIssues.title: Single-Core Variant Compatibility
topIssues.description: Tutorial uses xTaskCreatePinnedToCore which will fail on ESP32-C3 (single-core). Should mention using tskNO_AFFINITY for cross-compatibility.
topIssues.recommendation: Add note about single-core variants and tskNO_AFFINITY

topIssues.title: Stack Size Guidance
topIssues.description: Tutorial should explain how to determine appropriate stack sizes and warn about stack overflow issues common with FreeRTOS beginners.
topIssues.recommendation: Add section on choosing stack sizes

topIssues.title: Watchdog Timer Awareness
topIssues.description: No mention of Task Watchdog Timer (TWDT) which can trigger resets if tasks don't yield properly.
topIssues.recommendation: Add brief watchdog awareness section

topIssues.title: vTaskDelayUntil Not Mentioned
topIssues.description: For periodic tasks, vTaskDelayUntil() is more accurate than vTaskDelay() but isn't covered.
topIssues.recommendation: Mention vTaskDelayUntil for periodic task accuracy

topIssues.title: pdMS_TO_TICKS Macro
topIssues.description: Should recommend pdMS_TO_TICKS() over manual division for millisecond delays.
topIssues.recommendation: Recommend pdMS_TO_TICKS() macro for clarity

keep.reason: Clear explanation of RTOS benefits and task scheduling
Correct API usage for task creation
Proper infinite loop with delay pattern
Robo ESP32 with LED examples is appropriate
Task priority concepts are well explained
Coverage of ESP32's dual-core capabilities

update.action: Add note about tskNO_AFFINITY for portable code
Add section on choosing appropriate stack sizes
Recommend pdMS_TO_TICKS() and mention vTaskDelayUntil()

evidence.finding: FreeRTOS included in ESP32 Arduino Core by default
Works on dual-core, fails on ESP32-C3 with Invalid core ID
pdMS_TO_TICKS() is preferred for clarity and accuracy
TWDT monitors task execution, can cause resets
